shadows.name: hover-glow

shadows.name: inset-top-card

shadows.name: inset-top-input

shadows.name: auth-input-focus

shadows.name: anchor-flash

narrative.overview:
LLM Proxy's admin UI is an infrastructure instrument panel — a dark, monochrome console an operator reads mid-incident and trusts on the first glance. It pairs the discipline of editorial typography (Space Grotesk display, Manrope body, IBM Plex Mono for every number and code value) with the restraint of a telemetry surface: tonal layering, hairline borders, and ambient glow in place of ornament. The operator is technical, time-pressed, and often a stranger deploying the proxy for the first time, so the system earns trust through precision, not decoration.

The palette is monochrome editorial — deep cool-neutral voids in dark mode, crisp near-white in light mode — with a barely-perceptible hue tinting system reserved for semantic differentiation only: HTTP methods, status, and action types. Saturation is deliberately low; color never decorates, it disambiguates. The atmosphere is built from two fixed layers behind every screen: a trio of soft radial foreground-glints and a faint 42px grid masked toward the viewport center — present enough to read as a designed surface, quiet enough never to compete with data.

This system explicitly rejects the generic 2026 AI-tool aesthetic (cream/sand warm-neutral bodies, gradient-text headlines, identical icon-card grids, big-number hero-metric templates), loud SaaS gradients, playful/consumer affordances, and circa-2008 enterprise chrome. It is **dark-first**: dark mode is the primary experience and the canonical reference for every token below; light mode is a complete, first-class translation, not an afterthought.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first monochrome with cool-neutral (220°) undertones; light mode is a crisp mirror.
Editorial type pairing: geometric Space Grotesk display + humanist Manrope body + IBM Plex Mono for data.
Flat-by-default surfaces; depth via tonal background steps + 1px hairline borders, with ambient shadow only on the vestibule mark and transient toasts.
Low-saturation semantic tints (violet/blue/amber/rose/teal + status + syntax) — always paired with text or icon, never color-only.
Motion is exponential ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`), 150–500ms, GPU-only, and globally neutralized under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Tabular-numeric monospace for every metric, token count, cost, and timestamp.

Four structural grammars, chosen by task: the flush management console, the configuration form in a centered reading column, stacked hairline panels for personal settings, and the containerless vestibule (auth).
The 11px tracked uppercase label is a **label rail** — an in-panel micro-heading — never a page-section kicker.

rules.name: The Monochrome-First Rule
rules.body: Black, white, and the cool-neutral slate ramp carry 90%+ of any screen. The action/status tints are permitted only on badges, icon containers, metric values, and hover glows — never as section backgrounds, never as button colors (except `destructive`), never as large fills. If a screen reads as "colorful," it has failed this rule.

rules.name: The Tint, Not the Hue Rule
rules.body: Status and HTTP colors render at low alpha (`/15` background, `/25–30` border) with the full token as text. The badge is a labeled chip, not a swatch. Color is redundant information; the text label is the primary signal, and the chip is static — never a live region.

rules.name: The Cool-Neutral Undertone Rule
rules.body: Every surface, border, and mid-tone neutral carries hue 220° at very low chroma (3–14%). The extreme ink tokens (`--foreground`, `--primary`, `--ring`, `--sidebar-foreground`) may resolve to `0 0%` because hue is imperceptible at those lightnesses; those are the only true-gray values. Never introduce a true-gray mid-surface or a warm-neutral (`hue 30–100`) — both break the cool-console atmosphere and edge toward the cream/SaaS default this system rejects.

rules.name: The Quiet Syntax Rule
rules.body: The JSON and code palettes differentiate structure at low chroma for scanning — and only on code surfaces (JSON viewers, highlighted snippets, code blocks). Never reuse syntax tokens for badges, chart series, or fills; a rainbow syntax theme is a defect, not a feature.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Space Grotesk + Manrope + IBM Plex Mono is the whole system. Never introduce a fourth family. A number or code value set in Manrope is a defect, not a stylistic choice.

rules.name: The Mono-Data Rule
rules.body: Every numeric value — tokens, cost, latency, counts, timestamps, status codes, HTTP methods — is set in IBM Plex Mono with `tabular-nums`. Use `.text-data` inline and `.text-metric` for large stats.

rules.name: The Display Restraint Rule
rules.body: Display weight is 600 in-app, sizes cap at `text-2xl` (1.5rem) for page titles, and emphasis comes from weight + size in a single solid color — never from `background-clip: text` or a gradient.

rules.name: The Label-Rail Rule
rules.body: The 11px tracked uppercase label is a *rail*, not a *kicker*: it may sit **inside** a panel to name the value beneath it (spec-sheet cells, log-detail headings, segmented toggles, nav groups), and it never sits **above** a page or a page section to introduce content. If deleting it would leave the heading unable to say what follows, it was a kicker and does not belong.

rules.name: The One-Console Rule
rules.body: Management pages are one seamless surface — sticky header, flush toolbar, scrollable body — separated only by `border-b/60` hairlines. Never wrap a console table in an outer Card; never compete with the table's own thead.

rules.name: The Page-Header Anchor Rule
rules.body: Every route opens with exactly one `.page-header` (tinted icon container + `.brand-heading` title + muted description + actions). It is the consistent entry point a stranger trusts cold.

rules.name: The Task-Shape Rule
rules.body: Structure follows the task, not the page: management tables are one flush console; instance configuration is a centered form column under the console header; personal settings are stacked hairline panels; auth is containerless. Four grammars, one per task shape — never two on one screen.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only as a response to state (hover, elevation, focus) or as the constrained auth-mark and toast exceptions. Never pair a 1px border with a 16px+ blur drop shadow on the same element (the ghost-card pattern) — pick a tonal step or `shadow-xs`, never a wide decorative shadow.

rules.name: The Tonal-Step Rule
rules.body: When you need to separate two surfaces, step the background token (`--background` → `--card` → `--muted`) before reaching for a shadow. A 1px `--border` hairline plus a tonal step is the default depth recipe.

rules.name: The Radius Cap Rule
rules.body: Cards and panels cap at `rounded-xl` (16px). Save full-pill for tags and status chips; nav items use the control radius `rounded-md` (10px). No 24/28/32/40px card radii, no pill buttons.

rules.name: The No-Stripe Rule
rules.body: A colored >1px stripe never marks state anywhere in the system — active nav items are a filled `--sidebar-accent` step plus `font-medium`, and the only >1px rules are the neutral 2px console header bottom rules. Never use a colored `border-left/right` accent stripe on cards, list items, or alerts.

dos: Do set every numeric value — tokens, cost, latency, counts, timestamps, status codes — in IBM Plex Mono with `tabular-nums` (`.text-data` inline, `.text-metric` for large stats).

Do convey depth with tonal background steps (`--card` over `--background`, `--muted/5` page tint) and 1px `--border` hairlines; reserve shadow for `shadow-xs` at rest, ambient glow on hover, and the toast overlay exception.

Do render status and HTTP semantics as labeled `StatusBadge` chips at `/15` tint + `/25–30` border, with a text label as the primary signal; keep the chip static and leave live announcements to one result-count region.

Do use the `config-page-reveal` entrance on every page and the `stagger-fast` / `row-stagger` / `list-stagger` cascades on first render — and let the global `prefers-reduced-motion` rule neutralize them.
Do keep display tracking at −0.02em (floor −0.04em), display weight 600 in-app, and page titles at `text-xl sm:text-2xl`.
Do hit WCAG AA on both themes: tune `--muted-foreground` for readability, never lighten muted text "for elegance," and bump dark-mode body line-height to 1.55–1.6.

Do keep touch targets ≥44px (`min-h-11 min-w-11`) on nav, mobile controls, and every coarse-pointer viewport through the shared control-slot floor — tablets and touch laptops must clear 44px without enlarging mouse-driven desktop density.
Do render JSON and code with the syntax palette on code surfaces only — subtle chroma that reads as structure, never a rainbow theme.

Do build every pre-console screen through `AuthShell` and leave it containerless: one centered `max-w-sm` column, a 48px `auth-mark` locked up with the product name, 44px glass fields, and exactly one white CTA — the passkey button when the account has one, the password submit otherwise.

Do pick the structural grammar by task — flush console for management tables, full-width configuration headers with centered form columns for Settings and instance policy, stacked hairline panels in a centered column for personal settings, containerless for auth — and never mix two on one screen.
Do use the label rail *inside* a panel to name the value beneath it, and let a page heading stand without one.
donts: Don't make it playful/consumer — no cute illustrations, mascots, gamification, or celebratory confetti. This is infrastructure. *(PRODUCT.md anti-reference.)*
Don't ship boring/outdated admin panels — no dense gray-on-gray tables, no circa-2008 enterprise chrome, no cluttered "everything on one screen" dashboards. *(PRODUCT.md anti-reference.)*

Don't use loud color accents — no saturated SaaS gradients, no neon, no rainbow status badges. Color is a subtle low-saturation tinting system for semantic differentiation, never decoration. *(PRODUCT.md anti-reference.)*

Don't ship the generic 2026 AI-tool aesthetic — no cream/sand warm-neutral body backgrounds, no gradient-text headlines, no identical icon+heading+text card grids, no big-number hero-metric template. This is monochrome editorial, not warm SaaS. *(PRODUCT.md anti-reference.)*

Don't pair a 1px border with a 16px+ blur drop shadow on the same element (the ghost-card pattern). Pick a tonal step or `shadow-xs`, never a wide decorative shadow. The auth mark and toasts are the only ambient-shadow exceptions.
Don't over-round — cards and panels cap at `rounded-xl` (16px); save full-pill for tags and status chips; nav items use `rounded-md` (10px). No 24/28/32/40px card radii.
Don't use `border-left`/`border-right` greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards, list items, or alerts. State is a tonal step, never a stripe.

Don't use glassmorphism decoratively. `backdrop-blur` is limited to controls and transient overlays — `outline` buttons, inputs/input groups, floating tooltips, and full-screen media lightboxes — never a default card or page treatment. (`auth-mark` carries a gradient and a shadow, not a blur.)
Don't use `background-clip: text` with a gradient. Display emphasis comes from weight and size, in a single solid color.

Don't put a tiny uppercase tracked eyebrow above a page or a page section. The label rail belongs inside a panel, above the value it names; a kicker above a heading is the pattern this system does not use.
Don't set a metric or number in Manrope, or introduce a fourth type family. Space Grotesk + Manrope + IBM Plex Mono is the whole system.

Don't introduce true-gray (`0 0%`) mid-surfaces or warm-neutral (`hue 30–100`) tokens. Surface, border, and mid-tone neutrals carry the 220° undertone; only extreme ink tokens may sit at `0 0%` where hue is imperceptible.
Don't reuse the JSON/code syntax tokens outside code surfaces — no rainbow syntax themes, no syntax-colored badges or chart series.
Don't animate layout properties. Motion is `transform`/`opacity` only, exponential ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`), 150–500ms, with a reduced-motion alternative on every animation.
Don't give a static status or HTTP chip `role="status"`. A table of hundreds of rows must not mint hundreds of live-region announcers; the result-count region owns that job.
Don't wrap an auth form in a card, panel, or bordered container. The vestibule has no chrome — a card there turns a threshold into an object on a page.
Don't wrap a flush console table in an outer card, and don't give a stacked settings panel the console's sticky header bar. Each grammar is complete on its own.
